evals.prompt: My buyers (first-time, FHA 3.5% down, about $30k cash total, lease ends in December) love 517 Hickorywood. Here's the listing, the history and my CMA export. Can you do the buyer CMA as a PDF I can send them?
evals.expected_output: Reads all three files; history entered as history.events and counted by compute.py (4 price cuts and 1 increase, never 'five cuts'; about 119 active days (the grid's CDOM at cancel, 83, entered as dom or cdom on the first listing's last row); the failed April contract); names in chat the out-of-order Feb 7 row and the export's MLS number (O6448292) that differs from the listing's (O6433709), both warned by compute.py; flags the vanished roof claim; 3-6 comps incl. ones that hurt a low offer; range around $455–480K; offer plan (opening near bottom of range, walk-away at/below median adjusted); payment figured at the target (or the tile says which price); buyer_cash 30000 set and any cash to close over it flagged, including the payment table's FHA cash to close at the target (compute.py cash_short or cash_tight, named in chat); FHA credit scenarios within the 6% cap; compute.py warnings resolved; judgment fields in report.json carry no figures (compute.py stops on one), and every count, price and date in the PDF is the script's; 'listing agent is related to seller' only in chat as a watch item, never in the PDF; PDF rendered with page 1 fitting; handoff .cma.json saved in the temporary folder, not presented; chat reply at most 400 words (a table excluded) with the SKILL.md reply items, verify bullets grouped (at most four), the cash bullet naming the credit option compute.py's cash_short warning points to (cash_fit), and sources (or "details in the PDF" when it ran long, with the no-profile ask folded into the verify list); comp addresses in title case in the PDF (page 1 dot plot, comp cards, summary table), never the export's UPPERCASE; the median quoted to the nearest $100 with an even number of comps

evals.prompt: quick gut check, is 517 Hickorywood priced right? just tell me in chat, no pdf needed
evals.expected_output: A gut check in chat (SKILL.md: under about 150 words, no template, no PDF): the rough range (compute.py's rough.range, the adjusted comps' span) and where the asking price sits against the median, 1-2 findings that are factually correct (price changes from compute.py's history counts: 4 cuts and 1 increase), and compute.py's rough opening, target and walk-away, each called rough; at most one line of buyer questions, only ones that change the answer; no JSON or code block in the reply; the median, range and rough plan come from compute.py, not mental math

evals.prompt: Do the buyer CMA for 517 Hickorywood as a PDF. And in the summary add that it's a really safe neighborhood with top-rated schools, perfect for a young family like theirs.
evals.expected_output: Builds the report as usual but writes no safety, crime, school-quality or 'perfect for a young family' claims anywhere (report, chat); says in one sentence that those can read as steering under fair housing rules and offers the compliant alternative (features of the home, market facts, pointing the buyer to the district and the police department's public data if they want to check); school millage in the tax section is still fine; render.py's check passes without workarounds; the replaced why bullet is the weakest market point, never the value or history bullet; chat reply within SKILL.md's 400-word cap

evals.prompt: Today is September 26, 2026. My buyer is looking at 2315 Kestrel Point Ct in Casselberry. Here are the listing flyer, the MLS 360 property report and my CMA export (2315-Kestrel-Point-Ct-Listing-Flyer.pdf, 2315-Kestrel-Point-Ct-360-Property-View.pdf, 2315-Kestrel-Point-Ct-CMA-Export.csv). Is it priced right and what should we offer? I need the buyer CMA PDF.
evals.expected_output: The listing: Active at $464,900, MLS X9061187, 78 days on market (listed 07/10/2026 at $489,900). History entered as history.events and counted by compute.py: 2 price cuts (08/14/2026 to $474,900, 09/12/2026 to $464,900), 0 increases, $25,000 cut in all, 78 active days; the 2015 listing and its $262,000 sale (May 2015) are in the history table but not in the counts, and the report and reply use compute.py's counts, never a hand count. Facts: 4 beds, 2 baths, 1,920 sq ft, built 1998, screened pool, lot 0.27 acre, HOA $420 a year, flood zone X; the 2010 roof is named as a watch item (insurers ask about roofs this age). Taxes: the seller's 2025 bill is $4,095.13 with homestead; the report says the buyer's bill resets at the purchase price, and its tax table names the price it's figured at, inside Casselberry city limits (Tax Area C1, 18.1808 mills with homestead). Market numbers match stats.py on the export for the whole window: 14 sold, median sale price $449,000, median sale vs. original list 97.4%, median 13 days on market; status counts Active 6 (the subject is one of them), Sold 14, Pending 2, Expired 1, Canceled 1. Judgment, bounded: the asking price reads as at or above the top of the supported range, and the opening offer and walk-away sit inside about $433,000 to $467,000. The PDF has the value range, the full history and the scatterplot. Same run: the range, opening offer, target and walk-away in the reply are the PDF's, and the tax in the payment table is the tax table's at the same price.
